# Volume 3 — Chapter XIX An Interlude

!!! note "Source text"
    Passages cited on the wiki pages link into this page. Only volumes at or before
    this page's cutoff are present.

“It is amazing to realize that I am turning twenty today and have permanently bidden farewell to my teenage years,” remarked Nell, who sat huddled on the hearth-rug holding Smudge on her lap, addressing Aunt Euphemia, who was perusing a book in her favorite chair. Nobody else was present in the living room. Having departed for a committee meeting, Mabel and Honora were absent, while Cressy was in her room above dressing up for a social gathering.
{: #nw-v03-c19-p0000 }

“I imagine you feel a bit regretful,” Aunt Euphemia remarked. “One’s teenage years are a delightful period of existence. Personally, I am pleased that I have remained in them continuously.”
{: #nw-v03-c19-p0001 }

A laugh came from Nell.
{: #nw-v03-c19-p0002 }

“Aunty, you never are going to. You are going to be eighteen when a hundred ought to be your age. Indeed, I regret it, and I am also somewhat discontented. A long time back, Miss Thorne informed me that my character, whether for good or evil, would be shaped once I reached twenty. I do not sense that mine is as it ought to be. Imperfections fill it.”
{: #nw-v03-c19-p0003 }

“So’s everybody’s,” Aunt Euphemia said happily. “Mine has a hundred cracks in it. It is probable that your Miss Thorne was referring to how, by the age of twenty, a person's character has acquired a fixed inclination toward one way or another, after which it keeps evolving along those lines. Nell, do not stress about it. Fulfill what you owe to God, to those around you, and to yourself, while enjoying your life. Such is the doctrine I live by, and it has served me quite effectively. To what place is Cressy going this evening?”
{: #nw-v03-c19-p0004 }

“She is attending a dance, having acquired the most charming attire for the occasion—creamy yellow silk paired with lace like cobwebs. Those brown shades of hers are perfectly complemented by it.”
{: #nw-v03-c19-p0005 }

“‘Silk’ and ‘lace’ are magical terms, wouldn’t you agree?” Aunt Euphemia asked. “I feel like darting away to a ball at their mere utterance. As for yellow silk, it brings a gown made of sunlight to mind. A yellow silk dress was something I perpetually desired, yet my mother initially, and later my husband, refused to countenance it. Obtaining a yellow silk dress is the absolute first action I intend to take upon arriving in heaven.”
{: #nw-v03-c19-p0006 }

Cressy descended the stairs to the sound of Nell laughing heartily, draped in magnificent splendor, and examined her reflection within the wall’s tall oval glass.
{: #nw-v03-c19-p0007 }

“A mirror that flatters fosters a pleasant disposition,” she remarked. “The glass in my own chamber unquestionably gives me a green hue. Am I looking quite nice, Nell?”
{: #nw-v03-c19-p0008 }

“Are you truly aware of how lovely you look, Cressy?” inquired Nell, with genuine appreciation.
{: #nw-v03-c19-p0009 }

“Naturally I do. Why else do mirrors and men exist? That was not my point. Have all my ends been tucked in? Is the alignment of my skirt straight? Also, would a lower position suit this rose better? I am worried it is placed too high—it is going to give me a lopsided appearance. However, I detest having objects tickle my ears.”
{: #nw-v03-c19-p0010 }

“All is completely ideal, and your indentation on the southwest side is charming.”
{: #nw-v03-c19-p0011 }

“Nell, a specific quality I admire in you above all is your generosity—you lack even the smallest trace of envy.”
{: #nw-v03-c19-p0012 }

“What reason does she have to feel envy?” Aunt Euphemia asked. “Perhaps she isn't fully as attractive as yourself, yet the nose she possesses is considerably more handsome.”
{: #nw-v03-c19-p0013 }

“I am aware of that,” Cressy acknowledged.
{: #nw-v03-c19-p0014 }

“A source of immense solace has ever been my nose,” admitted Nell.
{: #nw-v03-c19-p0015 }

“And the manner in which your hair grows on your forehead is something I love, Nell. Also, that single tiny curl, which constantly appears about to fall yet never falls, is delightful. However, regarding noses, my own causes me terrible distress. I am certain that it will be Byrney once I reach forty. How do you imagine I will appear when I turn forty, Nell?”
{: #nw-v03-c19-p0016 }

“As if she were a mature, wedded, settled female,” poked fun Nell.
{: #nw-v03-c19-p0017 }

“I will not,” Cressy stated, making herself comfortable as she awaited her escort. “Joseph, you spotted little creature, stay off my lap. I refuse to attend a dance covered in cat hairs. No, Nell, I am not going to appear matronly. However, I shall certainly end up married.”
{: #nw-v03-c19-p0018 }

“Is it to Hector or Orlando?” Nell inquired.
{: #nw-v03-c19-p0019 }

“I guess it will be to one of those men,” Cressy sighed, “provided I am ever able to choose between them.”
{: #nw-v03-c19-p0020 }

“Deciding ought not to prove difficult,” Aunt Euphemia chided.
{: #nw-v03-c19-p0021 }

“My birth made me an oscillating Aunty, and there is no way I will ever be stopped from swaying.”
{: #nw-v03-c19-p0022 }

“Cressida, you should possess greater composure.”
{: #nw-v03-c19-p0023 }

“Naturally, maintaining composure is preferable,” concurred Cressida, “yet you lose out on a great deal of enjoyment. Regarding Hector and Orlando, being acquainted with them would make you comprehend the challenge in selecting one over the other. Their pleasantness is identical.”
{: #nw-v03-c19-p0024 }

“In that case, choose a person who is kinder,” Aunt Euphemia proposed. “Look at that Senior who is so attached to you—Will Lorna. His eyes are so wonderfully big, pleasant, and gentle.”
{: #nw-v03-c19-p0025 }

“Cruelly, Cressy remarked that they resembled a cow’s, being somewhat excessively big and gentle.”
{: #nw-v03-c19-p0026 }

“What is your opinion regarding Laurence Tibbs?”
{: #nw-v03-c19-p0027 }

“No more can be said regarding him, save that he constantly appears as though he were recently starched and ironed.”
{: #nw-v03-c19-p0028 }

“Then there is Marr Holworthy. No one could possibly fault him.”
{: #nw-v03-c19-p0029 }

“No, he would be acceptable if he were not lacking money. I have to wed a wealthy gentleman, Aunt Euphemia. That requirement—along with handsome features—is essential. I would wed Hugh Carrow were he wealthy.”
{: #nw-v03-c19-p0030 }

“Oh, do you think so?” Nell inquired, speaking with a bite of venom.
{: #nw-v03-c19-p0031 }

“Even though Hugh isn't someone we desire for ourselves, oh, no, we dislike that notion immensely,” Cressy taunted. “However, we should avoid discussing unpleasant topics. Sometime or another, I will likely be forced to wed, yet I intend to delay that unfortunate moment for as long as possible.”
{: #nw-v03-c19-p0032 }

“Ultimately, Cressy, you should not take anyone as a husband unless you love them,” Aunt Euphemia said.
{: #nw-v03-c19-p0033 }

“‘Ah, the affection that once filled devoted souls Has faded from popularity for a very long time.’”
{: #nw-v03-c19-p0034 }

tweeted Cressy tauntingly. “There is the carriage. I am off—Bi-bi, you pair of old-fashioned darlings.”
{: #nw-v03-c19-p0035 }

After Cressy departed, Aunt Euphemia cast a serious gaze upon Nell.
{: #nw-v03-c19-p0036 }

“That girl is lovely, gentle, and kind, but, Nell, do you believe she is fully sane at times?”
{: #nw-v03-c19-p0037 }

“Oh, I doubt anything is wrong with Cressy’s head,” Nell remarked, suppressing a grin. “That is merely how she speaks.”
{: #nw-v03-c19-p0038 }

Her head was shaken by Aunt Euphemia.
{: #nw-v03-c19-p0039 }

“Well, Nell, I do hope that is true, since I am in love with her. However, I fail to comprehend her—she completely baffles me. She differs from every girl I have ever known, as well as every girl that I used to be.”
{: #nw-v03-c19-p0040 }

“Aunt Phemie, how many girls were in your family?”
{: #nw-v03-c19-p0041 }

“Around six of them, my darling.”
{: #nw-v03-c19-p0042 }
